extraction_note: unit_of_analysis: 'article' closest to 'article/story cluster and news outlet'; no enum for story-cluster or outlet. interactivity: 'inspectable-drilldown' chosen as closest; product has rich comparison UI (Blindspot side-by-side, bias distribution per story, browser extension) beyond a simple drilldown — see schema gap 1. automation_level 'hybrid': aggregation is automated but bias ratings come from human-rated third-party agencies (Media Bias/Fact Check, AllSides, Ad Fontes).

persistent_knowledge_reuse: 'structured-KB-with-provenance' because the scite index (1.6B+ Smart Citations, 300M+ articles) carries provenance per citation statement, but is NOT dependency-tracked — closest enum without modification. access_model: freemium is primary; institutional licenses ($5,000-$25,000/yr) also exist per LibGuides — multi-value not representable in enum. Pricing figure from third-party review (visionsparksolutions.com), marked inferred; verify against scite.ai pricing page before proposal.

coverage_domain: 'political-claims' chosen; report specifies US politics specifically. evidence_quality_metadata: 'none' because sourcing is narrative/on-the-record, not systematic study-level or source-level credibility ratings. automation_level: 'human' per three-editor panel vote described by WRAL.

product: Penn Media Bias Detector (CSSLab / Duncan Watts)
extraction_note: symmetric_contrasting_evidence: mapped to 'yes' but report says 'partial' — compares publishers across ideological spectrum on a topic, NOT supporting/contrasting evidence per claim; see schema gap 7. claim_decomposition: 'none' in the entailment sense; product extracts/classifies 'facts' per article via LLMs but the CHI '25 paper does not describe premise decomposition. automation_level: 'fully-automated' LLM analysis with expert consultation per penntoday; undergraduate RA monitoring is QA, not primary automation.

claim_decomposition: 'none' because Factiverse does automatic claim *detection* (identifies check-worthy sentences), not decomposition into load-bearing premises; see schema gap 6. verdict_behavior: 'rates-sources-only' chosen over 'issues-verdicts' because the core product surfaces supporting/disputing sources; report notes veracity prediction appears in benchmarks but the primary product UI is source-surfacing. access_model: pricing figure (~$10.86/mo) from aggregator (theresanaiforthat.com), marked inferred; verify against factiverse.ai pricing before proposal. Vendor claim of 'outperforming GPT-4' is marketing-claim, not independently verified.

unit_of_analysis: 'claim' chosen; Perplexity's output is an answer-synthesis document with citations, not a formal claim/article/citation in the epistemic sense. verdict_behavior: 'transparency-only' chosen as closest; report says 'transparency-ish/synthesis — provides answer with citations, not a truth verdict'; product synthesizes an answer which slightly exceeds pure transparency-only. symmetric_contrasting_evidence: 'no' — report says 'sometimes presents multiple perspectives, not deliberate.' All cells except interactivity and coverage_domain are inferred from secondary sources.

claim_decomposition: 'none' because Originality.ai automatically *identifies* factual statements but does not decompose a composite claim into premises; see schema gap 6. access_model: 'freemium' chosen as closest for subscription/credit-based model; 'subscription' is not an enum value. Vendor claim of 86.69% accuracy is a marketing-claim, not independently verified.

unit_of_analysis: 'claim' used as closest enum; Wolfram Alpha's input is a computational/factual query, not an epistemic claim — see schema gap 3. coverage_domain: 'general' used as closest; Wolfram's domain is computational facts (math, science, geography, finance) — see schema gap 4. verdict_behavior: 'issues-verdicts' because Wolfram outputs authoritative computed answers; report notes these are 'not truth verdicts on contested claims' but there is no other fitting enum. persistent_knowledge_reuse: 'structured-KB-with-provenance' because the Wolfram Knowledgebase is curated from primary sources with continuous updating; NOT dependency-tracked. access_model pricing from third-party (futureaimind.com), marked inferred.

access_model: 'free' used as closest for open-source + Supporter Edition; 'open-source' enum does not exist — see schema gap 2. verdict_behavior: 'transparency-only' chosen because report says product 'withholds final judgment for the user'; automation_level 'hybrid' per human-in-the-loop design. NOTE: report flags this as 'the single closest existing system to Verity's decomposition + transparency ethic' but decomposes into *independent atomic claims*, not entailment-linked load-bearing premises, and has no persistent structured KB. ADVERSARY QUALIFICATION (H1): per report A, Loki issues a "human-in-the-loop verdict (semi-automated; withholds final judgment for the user)" — i.e., it does produce a verdict/credibility rating (report A H1: "it produces verdicts/credibility"); verdict_behavior='transparency-only' captures the withholding-from-user aspect but understates that a verdict is ultimately produced. Enums cannot fully express this; qualification encoded here per check instructions.

SAFE is a research evaluator, not a consumer product; interactivity='static' because no interactive UI exists (code library/API). evidence_quality_metadata: 'source-level' as closest — SAFE retrieves web documents and rates each fact supported/not-supported/irrelevant but does not expose study design or retraction flags. access_model: 'free' as closest for open-source GitHub release — see schema gap 2.

FActScore is an evaluation metric/library, not a consumer product; interactivity='static'. evidence_quality_metadata: 'none' because it produces only binary supported/unsupported (no study design, retraction, or source-credibility rating). persistent_knowledge_reuse: 'none' because FActScore does not maintain a KB — it grounds against Wikipedia at query time.

FEVER is an academic benchmark (Thorne et al. NAACL 2018), not a consumer product. All cells inferred from report A's brief mention in the 'Additional systems' section; more detail is in report B. The URL https://aclanthology.org/2020.emnlp-main.609 in sources_a.md is labeled '(FEVER)' but EMNLP 2020 is SciFact's venue, not FEVER (NAACL 2018) — likely a labeling error in the source file; no verified FEVER-specific URL used here.

SciFact is a benchmark dataset/system (Wadden et al. EMNLP 2020), not a consumer product. evidence_quality_metadata: 'source-level' because SciFact provides rationale sentences (evidence snippets from abstracts), not study design or retraction metadata.

claim_decomposition: 'none' despite AVeriTeC generating QA pairs as evidence — this is evidence retrieval structure, not premise decomposition of the target claim. symmetric_contrasting_evidence: 'no' despite the 'Conflicting Evidence/Cherry-picking' label — AVeriTeC issues a verdict (fourth category), it does not present symmetric transparency-only output. The 'knowledge store' is a benchmark artifact, not a reusable persistent KB.

Project wound down; interactivity='static' reflects current status. verdict_behavior: 'rates-sources-only' because Squash displayed existing fact-check ratings (from ClaimReview database), not original verdicts. automation_level: 'hybrid' because Squash's 'human Gardener' selected claim-to-fact-check matches. All cells inferred from Reporters Lab secondary sources.

access_model: 'institutional' because report describes Full Fact AI as 'internal/licensed tool'; not publicly available. All cells except automation_level inferred from limited secondary descriptions in report A.

access_model: 'institutional' chosen; Meedan Check is a tipline workflow tool used by news organizations, not a consumer product. verdict_behavior: 'rates-sources-only' because the tool surfaces fact-checks, not original verdicts. All cells inferred from brief report A description.

symmetric_contrasting_evidence: 'yes' per report's 'source breakdown showing support/contradict/partial' — partial symmetry, see schema gap 7. Vendor accuracy claims (logically.ai announcements) are marketing-claim confidence; verify before proposal. All cells inferred from limited secondary sources.

verdict_behavior: 'transparency-only' closest to impact voting (no truth verdict); the report notes Kialo uses 'pro/con nested argument trees with impact voting.' persistent_knowledge_reuse: 'none' in the KB-for-verification sense; Kialo persists human-authored arguments but does not reuse a fact-checking KB. Report describes Kialo as closest analog to Verity's argument-graph structure but fully manual.

scite Reference Check is a feature of scite.ai, not a standalone product; listed separately because report treats retraction-flagging tools as a distinct H7-relevant category. evidence_quality_metadata: 'study-level' because Reference Check flags retraction and editorial-concern status via Crossref/PubMed. Report note: 'direct-status only' — no propagation.

automation_level: 'hybrid' because Zotero alerts are automated but the library management itself is manual. persistent_knowledge_reuse: 'structured-KB-with-provenance' refers to Retraction Watch database via Crossref (structured, but NOT dependency-tracked). Report note: 'alerts on retracted items in library/citations; direct-status only' — one hop, no propagation.

interactivity: 'static' because RetractoBot delivers email notifications — no interactive UI. Report note: 'emails authors who cited a now-retracted paper (1-hop); no propagation.' All cells inferred from brief report A description.

access_model: 'API' chosen because Crossref Retraction Watch API is the primary mechanism; retractioncheck.com is a UI wrapper. Report note: 'federated retraction lookup only.' persistent_knowledge_reuse: 'structured-KB-with-provenance' for the Retraction Watch database via Crossref (structured with provenance, NOT dependency-tracked).

RedacTek is the closest deployed approximation to H7 (dependency-propagated invalidation), but operates at PAPER level across three citation generations (primary/secondary/tertiary), NOT claim-level invalidation. verdict_behavior: 'rates-sources-only' because the output is a paper-level 'issue association value' / 'retraction association value', not a claim verdict. All cells inferred from the Doody's Collection Development Monthly review (third-party); verify before proposal.
